title: Trả lại cổ vật · Problems / Solutions
prompt: Some societies are considering returning disputed cultural objects to their countries of origin. What problems could this create, and what measures could be taken to address them?
instructions: Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience. Write at least 250 words.

grammar.pattern: Publishing ... would help ..., while involving ... prevents ...
grammar.example: Publishing a timetable for examining disputed evidence would help distinguish a legitimate unresolved claim from repeated administrative delay, while involving the relevant communities prevents negotiation between states from silently excluding the people most closely connected to the object.
grammar.why: Publishing và involving đều là cụm danh động từ làm chủ ngữ, nhưng tác động khác nhau: lịch xử lý phân biệt tranh chấp với trì hoãn, sự tham gia cộng đồng ngăn thương lượng cấp nhà nước gạt chủ thể di sản ra ngoài.

paragraphs: Disputes over museum objects concern authority over historical interpretation as well as the physical location of a collection. The main problem is that broad demands based only on present borders can obscure complex ownership histories; decisions should examine provenance carefully and allow cooperative arrangements where claims overlap.

Broad demands based only on present borders can obscure complex ownership histories. Ownership histories can involve several communities and changing political boundaries, so present national location is not always a sufficient guide to entitlement. An object made by a community divided across modern borders could be claimed by two states, neither of which automatically represents all the people whose history gives the object its significance. A general rule based only on origin may replace one simplified account of ownership with another, leaving competing legitimate claims unresolved.

Decisions should examine provenance carefully and allow cooperative arrangements where claims overlap. A provenance panel could examine acquisition records alongside testimony from affected communities and publish reasons for its decision, using shared custody where entitlement overlaps rather than assuming that present national borders settle the claim. Publishing a timetable for examining disputed evidence would help distinguish a legitimate unresolved claim from repeated administrative delay, while involving the relevant communities prevents negotiation between states from silently excluding the people most closely connected to the object. Provenance research should involve affected communities and distinguish conflicting claims from mere inconvenience, so a request for further study does not become indefinite postponement. Decisions should examine provenance and the standing of affected communities, using cooperative arrangements where claims genuinely overlap rather than as an automatic substitute for justified restitution.

Restitution is strongest when it repairs a documented wrong and restores a community's voice; where entitlement is genuinely shared, cooperation should recognise that complexity without turning uncertainty into a permanent excuse for retaining every disputed object.

Coherence & Cohesion: đã giải thích cơ chế và điều kiện? Không lấy biên giới ngày nay làm bằng chứng sở hữu duy nhất. Nguồn gốc giao dịch, cộng đồng liên quan và thay đổi quốc gia có thể tạo yêu cầu chồng lấn.
Lexical Resource: dùng “provenance” đúng nghĩa “lịch sử nguồn gốc, sở hữu và chuyển giao của một hiện vật”, không thay thuật ngữ chính xác bằng từ hoa mỹ?
Grammar: can/could/may thể hiện khả năng chứ không chứng minh quan hệ nhân quả; mệnh đề điều kiện có nêu đúng điều kiện trong tình huống không?
